title: Prime-to-ell uniformization reduces to marked nodal quotient models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. Consider the following assertion about marked nodal quotient models. Let $Y$ be an affine integral excellent regular Noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension, with $\ell$ invertible, and let $T\subseteq Y$ be the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. Let $G$ be a finite group of order a power of $\ell$. Let $b:Y'\to Y$ be finite, with $Y'$ integral excellent and normal, such that, for $V=Y\setminus T$, $V'=b^{-1}V\to V$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor and $Y'$ is the normalization of $Y$ in its function field $\kappa(V')$. Let $f:C\to Y'$ be a $G$-equivariant projective flat finitely presented morphism, with $C$ integral excellent separated Noetherian, whose geometric fibres are nonempty connected curves smooth except for ordinary double points, and which is smooth over $V'$. An ordinary double point has completed geometric fibre ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Let $D\subset C$ be a $G$-stable effective Cartier divisor, finite etale over $Y'$ and contained in the smooth locus of $f$. Assume the action on $C$ is admissible, meaning every orbit lies in an affine open, and let $\pi:C\to X=C/G$ be its finite scheme quotient, with $X$ integral excellent Noetherian. Scheme quotient here means the orbit-space quotient, with structure sheaf $(\pi_*\mathcal O_C)^G$. Put $B=|D|\cup f^{-1}b^{-1}T$. Let $E\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor such that $\pi^{-1}|E|\subseteq B$. The assertion is that there are an integral regular Noetherian scheme $R$ and a proper birational morphism $r:R\to X$ for which $r^{-1}|E|$ is the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. Birational means inducing an isomorphism on dense open subschemes.

If this assertion holds for every such marked nodal quotient model, then for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $S$ with $\ell$ invertible and every nowhere dense closed subset $Z\subset S$, there is a finite covering family $(q_i:T_i\to S)$ in the topology of $\ell'$-alterations, with each $T_i$ regular Noetherian and $q_i^{-1}Z$ the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. In particular $q_i$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, hence of finite type.

Conventions: schemes, reduced schemes, Noetherian rings, excellence, regularity, integral schemes, properness, finite type and effective Cartier ideals are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]; boundaries and alteration coverings are as in [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Finite morphisms, projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, etaleness, geometric fibres, normalization, Galois torsors and Krull dimension are as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sc-normalization], [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Separated means that the diagonal into $C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}C$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product]. Normalization in the indicated finite extension $L$ of the function field means the scheme obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the integral closure of each affine coordinate domain in $L$; thus the extension field, rather than just the original function field, is used.

source.place: Expose IX, proof of Theorem 1.1, 1.3--1.4, printed pp. 132--133; the reduction uses Expose III Proposition 6.2 (pp. 43--45), Expose V 3.1.3--3.1.4 (p. 66), and the equivariant nodal model of IX Theorem 1.2 (p. 131). This is the conditional reduction before IX 2.1--2.4, not the conclusion of IX 1.1.

proof.text: Assume the marked nodal quotient assertion in the statement, for this fixed $\ell$. Write $U(S,Z)$ for the finite regular alteration-cover assertion in the conclusion. We first prove $U$ for all reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian schemes of dimension at most $d$, by strong induction on $d$. At each stage [lem-per-uniformization-complete-local-descent], in its bounded form, reduces the assertion to normal complete local schemes of dimension at most $d$. Thus the induction hypothesis is available for arbitrary excellent bases of dimension less than $d$, not merely complete local ones. After proving all finite stages we apply the unbounded form of that same descent theorem to the original $S$. This is legitimate because every Noetherian complete local ring has finite Krull dimension. No bound on the dimension of the original $S$ is imposed.

For a normal complete local scheme of dimension zero the local domain is a field, so the nowhere dense closed subset is empty and the identity is a regular covering with empty boundary. In dimension one [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes its local ring a discrete valuation ring; hence it is regular. A proper closed subset is empty or its closed point. In the latter case a uniformizer defines that reduced point, a strict normal crossings boundary with one regular component of codimension one. The identity is the required cover. These exhaust the dimensions zero and one.

Let $d\geq2$ and take a normal complete local $X$ of dimension $d$, with its prescribed nowhere dense $Z$. Apply [lem-per-prime-to-ell-marked-algebraization] to get $p:X^+\to X$, $g:X^+\to W$, the marked pair $(W,Z_W)$, and the regular complete local base $Y_0$ of dimension $d-1$. The morphism $p$ is a covering: it is finite surjective with generic degree prime to $\ell$. It will suffice to construct $U(W,Z_W)$, pull its covering back by the regular completion map $g$ using [lem-per-regular-pair-alteration-pullback], and compose with $p$. That lemma preserves both regularity and the exact inverse-image support. In particular this reduction does not treat completion as a finite-type object of $\operatorname{alt}/W$; only the pulled-back finite-type covering maps are objects of $\operatorname{alt}/X^+$.

Apply [lem-per-proper-generic-curve-preparation] to $W\to Y_0$ and $Z_W$. Its zero-dimensional generic-marking hypothesis holds: $W$ is integral, its generic fibre has dimension one, and a nowhere dense closed subset cannot contain that fibre's generic point. We obtain $f:P\to Y_1$, the effective Cartier marking $E$, and $h:P^\circ\to W$ of generic degree prime to $\ell$. The base $Y_1$ is affine integral normal excellent of dimension at most $d-1$; the generic fibre of $f$ is smooth geometrically integral, and $E$ is generically finite etale. Proving $U(P,|E|)$ suffices: restrict the resulting cover to $P^\circ$, where its boundary is the inverse image of $h^{-1}Z_W$, and compose with the covering $h$. Open restriction preserves the regular local rings and the defining boundary intersections.

source.place: IX 1.3, p. 132, compactification through Stein factorization

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-equivariant-marked-nodal-alteration] to $(P\to Y_1,E)$, obtaining $C\to Y'$ and $G$. Replace $P$ by $Q=C/G$ and the base by $Y=Y'/G$. The maps $Q\to P$ and $Y\to Y_1$ are proper birational. The former is a covering of generic degree one. Pull $E$ back to $Q$: its equation stays nonzero on the integral dominant source, hence still cuts out an effective Cartier divisor. The marking inclusion above $E$ is precisely the one supplied by the nodal theorem. The new $Y$ is integral excellent and has dimension at most $d-1$: it is proper birational over the excellent finite-dimensional $Y_1$ [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension]. Its separatedness over the affine original base permits finite affine open refinement. All group actions are admissible. We henceforth work separately over those affine opens and use $X=C/G$ for the quotient total space.

Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $H\leq G$ using [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index]. The action on $C$ is generically free, since any stabilizer maps to a stabilizer on the dense free locus of $Y'$, and $C\to Y'$ is dominant. Both $C$ and $Y'$ are of finite type over the affine excellent base of Step 5, on which $G$ acts trivially, so [lem-per-admissible-quotient-generic-degree] applies to them; by it the finite surjective map $C/H\to C/G$ has generic degree $[G:H]$, prime to $\ell$, so it is a covering. Replace $G$ by $H$, $X$ by $C/H$ and $Y$ by $Y'/H$. The base is still affine integral excellent and finite over the preceding base, so has dimension at most $d-1$ by [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension]. Pull back the Cartier marking; the support inclusion persists. The original $T'$ remains $H$-stable and its complement has free $H$-action. Apply [lem-per-free-finite-action-torsor] to that open to obtain a finite etale $H$-torsor over the complement of $T=T'/H$. Thus $G$ is now an $\ell$-group. These replacements never require a prime-to-$\ell$ degree for $C\to X$ itself.

Apply the induction hypothesis to $(Y,T)$, whose dimension is at most $d-1$. It supplies a finite covering $(Y_i\to Y)$ with $Y_i$ regular and the exact inverse image $T_i$ a strict normal crossings support. Each retained integral component $Y_i$ dominates $Y$ and is generically finite over it, by the definition of the alteration category. Thus $\dim Y_i\leq\dim Y\leq d-1$ by the inequality in [lem-trf-closed-dominant-dimension]. Refine by finitely many affine opens and connected components; the resulting bases are integral excellent regular Noetherian. Here excellence follows from finite type over the excellent $Y$ [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], and regular connected Noetherian schemes are integral [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]. Apply [lem-per-nodal-quotient-normalized-base-refinement] to these maps: normalize a dominating component of $Y'\times_Y Y_i$, choose its decomposition subgroup $G_i$, and pull the nodal curve and marking to that normalized base. The resulting quotients $X_i=C_i/G_i$ cover $X$ in the alteration topology. The cited statement supplies the entire comparison with the dominant pullback, including proper birationality, so no equality between normalization and ordinary base change is presumed.

source.place: IX 1.4, p. 133, induction and normalized components

proof.text: For each $i$, all hypotheses of the assumed marked nodal quotient assertion now hold: $Y_i$ is affine integral excellent regular Noetherian of finite dimension, $T_i$ is an snc support; $G_i$ is a subgroup of an $\ell$-group; $Y'_i$ is finite and is exactly the normalization of the connected $G_i$-torsor off $T_i$; $C_i$ is integral excellent separated Noetherian and projective flat finitely presented with the required connected nodal fibres; and $D_i$ is stable, finite etale and in the smooth locus. These clauses and admissibility are supplied by [lem-per-nodal-quotient-normalized-base-refinement]. The pulled-back $E_i$ is Cartier and its inverse image lies in the marked vertical boundary. Therefore the hypothesis produces a proper birational $r_i:R_i\to X_i$ with $R_i$ integral regular Noetherian and the exact inverse image of $|E_i|$ an snc support. Each $r_i$ is a singleton covering, of generic degree one.

source.place: IX 1.4, p. 133, situation (*) and the assumed resolution of that situation

proof.text: Compose these finitely many $r_i$ with the covering $X_i\to X$ and then all previous coverings; restrict over $P^\circ$ to get a finite regular covering of $(W,Z_W)$. Pull back by $g:X^+\to W$ and compose with $p:X^+\to X$. Cover calculus gives finite covering families throughout, and regular pullback gives the same snc support as the full inverse image of $Z$. This proves the complete-local case in dimension $d$; the bounded descent theorem completes the induction. Every complete normal local Noetherian scheme has finite dimension, so unbounded complete-local descent now gives $U(S,Z)$ for the original reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian $S$. By the definition of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, all final arrows are finite type. No equation for $Z$ on the original $S$ was required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q74-58e0fb335 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all nine new nodes and every cited statement in full. Sources checked in ILO: IX 1.1-1.4 (pp.131-133), III 6.1-6.2 with proof (pp.43-45), V 2.1.1-2.1.2 and 3.1.1-3.1.4 (pp.64-66), II 1.2.5-1.2.9 and 2.1-2.3.4 (pp.25-28). The statement is unchanged against the base copy and no SGA is cited. Steps 1-9 follow IX 1.3-1.4: (1) III 6.2 descent; the proof of 6.2 already reduces to normal complete local rings, and the bounded form holds because henselization and completion keep the dimension. (2) Dimensions 0 and 1 are a field and a DVR. (3) V 3.1.3/3.1.4 algebraization. Shrinking to the normal component through w, dominance, generic fibre dimension 1, nowhere-density of Z_W and regularity of g all hold. Pullback by g is II 2.3.4 with 031E. (4) IX 1.3 preparation.
